summary: Vina's lookout station was replaced after lightning in 1961, then demolished in 2018 for a new Cal Fire helitack base that operates today.

facts.design: Fire station with a cupola (a firefinder inside) and barracks; the 1961 replacement was virtually identical to the original
facts.status_note: The station and lookout were demolished in 2018; the site is now an operating Cal Fire helitack base.
facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection - Tehama-Glenn Unit (Cal Fire TGU)

events.note: Original station and lookout, dated circa 1954 by the register. The Chico paper gives 1955 for the base.
Original station and lookout destroyed by lightning
Replacement station, virtually identical to the original; the register's Built field gives 1961
Base updated for helicopters; Cal Fire describes it as an operational helitack base since 1974
Old station and buildings demolished to make way for a new helitack base
First in California to take delivery of the new Black Hawk; base then reported as year-round, 24-hour operation

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates the original station to about 1954 and gives 1961 for its replacement after lightning destroyed the original. The 2018 Chico paper says the base dates to 1955. The record's 1961 is the replacement's date, not the first station's. The 1954 and 1955 dates are not reconciled.

notes_for_editor: The record's KRCR link (krcrtv.com/news/butte-county/construction-underway-for-new-vina-helitack-base) returns HTTP 404 in our cache; drop or replace it. The record's kind two_story is not confirmed by any source read. No source read gives lookout staffing or fire history, so none is stated. The register's 'open to visitors' note is dated 1991 and predates the 2018 rebuild; no source confirms public access today. The 1954/1955 start date is unresolved. A Corning Observer article on the base's aircraft returned HTTP 429 and was not read.
